half-hours-with-great-story-tellers-arte:
Half-Hours with Great Story Tellers collects short fiction for readers who want a complete tale at a sitting. The volume is dated 1891. Its title page promises Artemus Ward, George Macdonald, Max Adeler, Samuel Lover, and others. The contents open with Barham's Grey Dolphin, a tale of a baron whose boots, once called for, spread consternation through Shurland Castle. Ward's Moses, the Sassy follows.

Dickens contributes Boots at the Holly-Tree Inn. MacDonald's fairy tale The Light Princess is the volume's centerpiece. A princess who cannot feel gravity, in body or mind, must learn sorrow to be saved. Lover's Legend of the Little Weaver and Adeler's Fate of Young Chubb fill out the set. Such anthologies were the period's short story course. Editors mixed humor, ghost, and fairy tale, trusting variety to hold a family audience for the half hour of the title.
